R11 — the localization dictionary's Huffman tree: serialisation pinned, alphabet vs usage, and whether a canonical rebuild
from the strings' own symbol histogram reproduces EA's tree (read-only; 2026-09-20, Priority 1C).

Per dictionary: tree bytes / node count / leaf alphabet; decoded symbol histogram over every reachable key and text (the Huffman-coded
bytes; length prefixes are raw and excluded); per-symbol code lengths from the file's tree vs optimal Huffman lengths for the histogram
(total coded bits, equal?); leaves that no string uses and symbols used that have no leaf (must be none); an attempt to regenerate the
exact tree bytes with a standard Huffman construction under several tie-break policies, serialised as observed (root = node 0; each
internal node is one 4-byte quad `left(marker, value) right(marker, value)`; a leaf child is `00 sym`; an internal child is
`<its node number> 00`; node numbers are assigned breadth-first with the RIGHT internal child enqueued before the LEFT).

Sources: the 25 committed anchors, the 100 private gen7 loose locale files (E:\nhl-studio-fixtures\loc\<platform>-<title>\*.db) and the
50 extracted PS4 locale files (H:\...\CUSA*\databigs\Extracted\nhl\data\kettle\loc\*.db).

Usage: python loc_tree_rebuild.py <out.json> [--only anchors|private|ps4] [--limit N]
